# Activepieces: Workflow Orchestration for a Personal AI Assistant

Citation-backed research evaluating Activepieces as a workflow engine for a
personal AI-assisted engineering assistant running on a single Fedora workstation.

## TL;DR

Activepieces is an MIT-licensed, self-hostable workflow automation platform that
**can execute arbitrary shell commands** in its default `UNSANDBOXED` execution
mode [6][11]. This satisfies the #1 requirement. It supports cron scheduling,
webhook triggers (enabling credential-isolated execution), and per-step debugging.
Compared to n8n, it trades performance (15-30x slower on simple tasks, ~6x on
concurrent workloads — both in sandboxed mode) and integration depth for a
genuinely open-source license and simpler setup.
Worth a hands-on trial — deploy the single Docker container and test a CLI
workflow via webhook.

## Requirements Assessment

| # | Requirement | Status | Notes |
|---|------------|--------|-------|
| 1 | Shell/CLI execution | **Met** | UNSANDBOXED mode: full Node.js + bash [6][11] |
| 2 | Credential isolation | **Met** | No retrieval API, masked in logs [14] |
| 3 | Self-hosted, single workstation | **Met** | Single Docker container option [8] |
| 4 | REST API management | **Partial** | 15 endpoint groups, but API keys may need Platform edition [15] |
| 5 | Scheduling | **Met** | Cron (Quartz), daily/weekly/monthly [Agent B] |
| 6 | Execution history | **Met** | Per-step I/O, 30-day retention [11][12] |
| 7 | Retry/error handling | **Partial** | 4 retries, no configurable backoff, no DLQ [18] |
| 8 | Webhook triggers | **Met** | GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, Basic/Header auth [Agent B] |
| 9 | Licensing | **Met** | MIT (OSI-approved) [3] |
| 10 | AI/LLM integration | **Met** | Universal AI pieces, MCP servers [19][2] |

## Quick Comparison: Activepieces vs n8n

| Dimension | Activepieces | n8n | Winner |
|-----------|-------------|-----|--------|
| License | MIT | Sustainable Use (not OSI) | AP |
| Ease of setup | G2: 9.1/10 | G2: 7.9/10 | AP |
| Shell execution | UNSANDBOXED mode | Code node (JS/Python) | Tie |
| Performance | 95 req/s (sandboxed) | 220+ req/s | n8n |
| Integrations | 200-450+ pieces (growing rapidly) | 500+ nodes | n8n |
| AI/LLM | Universal AI + MCP | 70+ LangChain nodes | n8n |
| Community | 21.6k stars | 150k+ stars | n8n |
| Workflow model | Linear (1 trigger) | Graph (multi-trigger) | n8n |

## Decision Framework

1. **Does UNSANDBOXED mode work for your CLI tools?** → Test with `gh pr list`
   in a Code piece triggered via webhook
2. **Is REST API needed beyond webhooks?** → If yes, check whether community
   edition provides API keys
3. **Is the performance gap acceptable?** → UNSANDBOXED mode was not benchmarked;
   actual gap for personal use may be smaller than the 15-30x sandboxed figure
4. **Does one-trigger-per-flow constrain your workflows?** → If complex
   branching is needed, n8n's graph model is more flexible
5. **Does the MIT license matter?** → If the project may evolve into something
   distributable, MIT provides more freedom
